newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end mostly down on liquidation.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end mostly down on liquidation.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly down on Tuesday on long liquidation as the Labour Day holiday approaches, traders said.
The most actively traded September 1997 contract ended at an intraday low of 3,345 yuan ($403) per tonne, losing 46 yuan. It opened at 3,370 yuan and hit a high of 3,379 yuan per tonne.
May fell nine yuan to 3,415, July rose 28 to 3,348, November dropped two to 3,398 and the January 1998 contract 10 to 3,400.
Combined volume rose to 17,300 tonnes from 9,800.
Soybeans opened mostly down and long liquidation pushed prices lower for most of the session, traders said.
"Investors continued to liquidate their long positions before the four-day Labour Day holiday," one trader said.
"Active trading on the rice futures market recently also attracted a lot of hot money," he added.
Traders said they expected soybeans not to drop further in the next few days due to a lack of market-moving news.
